title: Particle Accelerator Beam Collision Detector
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing an interactive 3D particle accelerator beam collision detector simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Dark scene with a black background (0x000000) and subtle ambient light (0x222244, intensity 0.3) plus a point light (0xaaccff, intensity 1.5) at (0, 10, 0).
- Camera at (0, 8, 25) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Load the 'Parrot.glb' model using GLTFLoader from '../../../assets/shared/Parrot.glb'. Scale it to 0.02 and position it at (0, 12, 0) as a decorative mascot hovering above the detector. Animate it with a gentle bobbing motion (sinusoidal Y offset, amplitude 0.5, period 2s). Store reference as window.__3D_STATE__.parrotModel.

## Accelerator Ring
- Create a TorusGeometry (radius 10, tube 0.3, segments 64) with emissive blue material (0x0044ff) as the main accelerator ring, lying flat in the XZ plane.
- Add a second inner torus (radius 7, tube 0.15) with emissive red material (0xff2200) as the counter-rotating beam pipe.

## Particle Beams
- Beam A: 50 small spheres (radius 0.08, emissive cyan 0x00ffff) orbiting clockwise along the outer ring at angular velocity controlled by beamEnergy.
- Beam B: 50 small spheres (radius 0.08, emissive magenta 0xff00ff) orbiting counter-clockwise along the inner ring.
- Both beams start stationary. Particles are evenly distributed around their respective rings.
- beamEnergy starts at 0.0 (range 0.0 to 10.0). Angular velocity = beamEnergy * 0.5 rad/s.

## Collision System
- A collision zone is defined at angle=0 (positive X axis) with an angular tolerance of 0.1 radians.
- When beamEnergy >= 5.0 and the simulation is running, collisions can occur. A collision triggers every time a Beam A particle and Beam B particle are both within the collision zone simultaneously.
- Each collision produces 3-8 random debris particles (small yellow spheres, radius 0.04) that fly outward from the collision point with random velocities (speed 2-6 units/s). Debris particles fade out over 2 seconds (opacity 0 at end) and are removed.
- Track totalCollisions (integer count) and totalDebrisProduced (integer count).

## Energy & Momentum Conservation
- Define system total energy = beamEnergy * 100 (beam kinetic) + debris count * 2 (debris energy). Track as totalSystemEnergy.
- When a collision occurs, beamEnergy decreases by 0.05 per collision (energy transferred to debris). Minimum beamEnergy is 0.0.
- Track momentumX and momentumY of all active debris particles. Since beams collide head-on, net debris momentum should be near zero (within +/-5.0 tolerance for each axis due to randomness).

## Detector Panels
- Place 8 flat rectangular panels (BoxGeometry 3x4x0.1) arranged in an octagon around the collision zone at radius 14, facing inward. These are detector panels.
- Each panel has a hit counter. When a debris particle reaches radius >= 13 from center, the nearest panel's hitCount increments and the panel flashes white briefly (0.3s).
- Store panel data as detectorPanels array of {id, hitCount, angle}.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left HUD overlay showing: Beam Energy (1 decimal), Total Collisions, Total Debris Produced, Simulation Status (STOPPED/RUNNING/PAUSED).
- A 'Start' button (id='btn-start') that begins the simulation (sets running=true).
- A 'Pause' button (id='btn-pause') that toggles pause (sets paused flag).
- A 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') that resets everything to initial state: beamEnergy=0, collisions=0, debris cleared, particles back to start positions, status=STOPPED.
- An energy slider (id='slider-energy', type=range, min=0, max=10, step=0.1) to set beamEnergy. Only works when simulation is running and not paused.
- A 'Toggle Detector View' button (id='btn-detector-view') that toggles showing/hiding a DOM table (id='detector-table') listing each panel's ID and hit count.

## Keyboard Controls
- Space: toggle pause (same as pause button)
- R: reset (same as reset button)
- ArrowUp: increase beamEnergy by 0.5 (clamped to 10.0), only when running
- ArrowDown: decrease beamEnergy by 0.5 (clamped to 0.0), only when running
- D: toggle detector table visibility

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- simulationStatus: 'STOPPED' | 'RUNNING' | 'PAUSED'
- beamEnergy: number (0.0-10.0, 1 decimal precision)
- beamAParticleCount: number (50)
- beamBParticleCount: number (50)
- totalCollisions: integer
- totalDebrisProduced: integer
- activeDebrisCount: integer (currently live debris particles)
- totalSystemEnergy: number
- momentumX: number (net X momentum of active debris)
- momentumY: number (net Y momentum of active debris)
- detectorPanels: array of 8 objects {id: number, hitCount: number, angle: number}
- totalDetectorHits: number (sum of all panel hitCounts)
- detectorTableVisible: boolean
- parrotY: number (current Y position of parrot)
- parrotLoaded: boolean
- frameCount: integer (increments each animation frame)
- lastResetFrame: integer (frameCount at last reset)

Update __3D_STATE__ every animation frame.
physics_constraints: Beam angular velocity proportional to beamEnergy. Collisions only occur when beamEnergy >= 5.0 and simulation is RUNNING. Each collision reduces beamEnergy by 0.05. Net debris momentum should remain near zero (+/-5.0 per axis). Total detector hits must equal totalDebrisProduced that reached detector radius. Energy conservation: beam energy lost = debris energy gained approximately. All numerical values must be NaN-free.
